questions.question: The Great Stupa at Sanchi was built by ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Ashoka__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sanchi is a Buddhist complex**, famous for its **Great Stupa**, on a hilltop at **Sanchi Town in Raisen** **District** of the State of **Madhya Pradesh, India.**
 
• The Great Stupa at Sanchi is one of the **oldest stone structures** **in India** and an important monument of **Indian Architecture**.
 
• It was originally commissioned by the **emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE.**
 
• **Its nucleus was a simple hemispherical brick structure** built over the **relics of the Buddha**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ashoka is also known as Ashoka the Great, was an Indian emperor of the **Maurya Dynasty**, who ruled almost all of the Indian subcontinent from **268 to 232 BCE.**
 
• He was the grandson of the **dynasty's founder** **Chandragupta Maurya.**
 
• **Ashoka** promoted the **spread of Buddhism across ancient Asia. **

questions.question: Which among the following is known as the earliest period in history?
questions.solution:

• Mesolithic age was the middle stone age, which ended with the introduction of agriculture.
 
• Neolithic age was the new stone age where a lot of social development took place.
 
• Chalcolithic age was the copper age where early copper metallurgy appeared.

questions.question: Svetambara and Digambara are two sects of the _______ community.
questions.solution:
__
 
• Svetambara and Digambara are two sects of the **Jain community.**
 
• Svetambara Jains are **“those who wear white” **and is one of the two important sects of Jainism.
 
• Svetambaras unlike Digambaras do not believe in renunciation of clothes for attaining liberation.
 
• They also believe that anybody can attain liberation(including women).
 
• Digamabara Jains are those to whom** “space is the garment” **and **do not wear anything**.
 
• The *Digambara* Jains **worship completely nude idols** of ***tirthankaras* **(omniscient beings) and *siddha* (liberated souls). The *tirthankara* is represented either seated in yoga posture or standing in the ***Kayotsarga* **posture.
 
• They believe that** liberation can only be attained through male body** and **nudity is necessary** to break the bondage of illusory world.
 
• **Extra:-**__
 __
 
• ** Jainsim has 24 *teerthankaras ***(those who have conquered the illusory world and cycles of birth and death and those who lead others towards liberation)
 
• **Rishabnath was the first Jain teerthankar and the founder of Jainism.**
 
• **Mahavira was the last and 24th Jain teerthankar.**
 
• **Five main vows of Jainism:-**__
 
 

 
• ***ahiṃsā*** (non-violence),** *satya* **(truth), ***asteya*** (not stealing), ***brahmacharya*** (celibacy or chastity or sexual continence), and ***aparigraha***** **(non-attachment)

questions.question: The first battle of Tarain was fought between ___________.

options.text: Prithviraj Chauhan and Mohammad Bin Qasim

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prithviraj Chauhan and Muhammad Ghori**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The first battle of Tarain** was fought in 1191 CE near Thanesar, present-day Haryana.
 
• Prithviraj Chauhan was the king of Ajmer and Delhi, and Muhammad Ghori was the ruler of Ghurids in Afghanistan.
 
• The battle was fought between the Ghurids and the Chauhans over the control of the northwestern regions of India.
 
• The Chauhan army was led by Prithviraj Chauhan, while the Ghurid army was led by Muhammad Ghori himself.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Mohammad Bin Qasim was an Arab general who invaded Sindh in 712 CE, nearly 500 years before the first battle of Tarain. Hence, this option is incorrect.
 
• Mahmud Ghaznavi was a Turkish ruler who invaded India multiple times in the 11th century, but he did not participate in the first battle of Tarain. Hence, this option is incorrect.
 
• Qutubuddin Aibak was a slave-general of Muhammad Ghori who later became the first Sultan of Delhi after Ghori's death. He did not participate in the first battle of Tarain as he was not yet a prominent figure. Hence, this option is incorrect.

questions.question: Famous ruler Kanishka belonged to the ______ dynasty.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Kushan__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kanishka belonged to the Kushan dynasty__.
 
• The kushan dynasty was founded by Kujūla Kadphises.
 
• Kanishka ruled around the 1st century CE and was the greatest king of the Kushan dynasty.
 
• At the time of Kanishka, kushan rule was spread over the northern part of the Indian subcontinent, Afghanistan, and possibly areas of Central Asia north of the Kashmir region.
 
• He is also remembered as a great patron of Buddhism.
 
• He studied Buddhism under the Buddhist poet Ashvaghosha.
 
• The Fourth Buddhist Council was also convened under his patronage in Kashmir.
 
• That council compiled The Great Commentary on Abhidharma.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The Kushanas:

 
 
• The first Kushana dynasty was founded by Kujula Kadphises.
 
• Vima Kadphises issued gold coins in India.
 
• Kanishka founded the second Kushana dynasty.
 
• Their capitals were at Peshawar and Mathura.
 
• The most famous Kushana ruler was Kanishka, he was also known as ‘*Second Ashoka*’.
 
• He started an era in 78 AD which is now known as the Saka Era and is used by the Government of India.
 
• Kanishka was a great patron of Mahayana Buddhism.
 
• During his reign, the 4th Buddhist Council was held in Kundalavana, Kashmir where the doctrines of the Mahayana form of Buddhism were finalized.
 
• The last great Kushana ruler was Vasudeva I.
 
• The Kushanas were the first rulers in India to issue gold coins on a wide scale.

questions.question: Which two kings fought in the Battle of Hydaspes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alexander and Porus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In 326 BC, Alexander the Great** faced **King Porus in the Battle of the Hydaspes**, also known as the **Battle of Jhelum**.
 
• It took place on the banks of the** Jhelum River** (called as Hydaspes by the ancient Greeks) in the **Punjab area **of India (modern-day Punjab, Pakistan).
 
• The conflict ended with a Greek triumph and Porus' capitulation.
 
• Large swaths of Punjab were integrated into the Alexandrian Empire, and Alexander reinstalled the vanquished and dethroned Porus as a subordinate ruler.
 
• One of Alexander's "masterpieces" was his choice to cross the monsoon-swollen river despite intense Indian monitoring in order to catch Porus' army off-guard.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Alexander III of Macedon**, also known as** Alexander the Great,** was the monarch of Macedon in ancient Greece.
 
• At the age of 20, he succeeded his father Philip II to the throne in 336 BC and spent the majority of his reign executing a lengthy military campaign across Western Asia and Northeastern Africa.
 
• He had built one of the biggest empires in history by the age of thirty, ranging from Greece to northwestern India.
 
• **Porus** was an ancient Indian king whose kingdom stretched between the Hydaspes (Jhelum River) and the Acesines (Chenab River) in the Punjab area of India.

questions.question: Which of the following varnas was responsible for protecting people and administering justice in ancient India as per rules laid down by the Dharmasutras and Dharmashastras?
questions.solution:
• The Dharmasutras and Dharmashastras also contained rules about the ideal “occupations” of the four categories or varnas.
 
• **Brahmanas were supposed to study and teach the Vedas,** perform sacrifices and get sacrifices performed, and give and receive gifts.
 
• **Kshatriyas were to engage in warfare, protect people and administer justice,** study the Vedas, get sacrifices performed, and make gifts.
 
• The last three “occupations” were also assigned to the **Vaishyas**, who were in addition expected to** engage in agriculture, pastoralism and trade.**
 
• **Shudras **were assigned only one occupation – that of **serving the three “higher” varnas**.
 
• The Brahmanas evolved two or three strategies for enforcing these norms. One, as we have just seen, was to assert that the varna order was of divine origin.
 
• Second, they advised kings to ensure that these norms were followed within their kingdoms.
 
• And third, they attempted to persuade people that their status was determined by birth. However, this was not always easy. So prescriptions were often reinforced by stories told in the Mahabharata and other texts.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is "__**Third Buddhist Council – Pataliputra**__".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• **Six Buddhist Councils marked important **turning points in the story of **early Buddhism.**
 
• This story spans the time from immediately after the death and Parinirvana of the** historical Buddha in the 5th century BCE** to sometime early in the first millennium CE.
 
• This is also the story of sectarian clashes and the eventual Great Schism that resulted in the **two major schools,** **Theravada** and **Mahayana**.
 
• In total, **6 Buddhist councils **were convened.

**The description of the six Buddhist councils has been given below:**

**First Buddhist Council :**

 
• It was held soon after the **Mahaparinirvan** of the **Buddha, around 483 BC** under the patronage of** King Ajatshatru.**
 
• It was presided by Mahakasyapa, a monk. The council was held in the Sattapani cave at Rajgriha.
 
• The council was held with the purpose of preserving Buddha’s teachings (Sutta) and rules for disciples. During this council, the teachings of Buddha were divided into three Pitakas.
 
• The significance of the First Council is that 500 senior monks adopted the Vinaya-Pitaka and Sutta-Pitaka as the accurate teaching of the Buddha, to be remembered and kept by generations of nuns and monks to come.

 

**Second Buddhist Council :**

 
• The Second Buddhist Council was held at **Vaisali (or Vaishali), **an ancient city in what is now the **state of Bihar in northern India,** bordering Nepal under the patronage of King Kalasoka while it was presided by Sabakami.
 
• This Council probably was held about a century after the first one, or about 383 BCE.
 
• It was called to discuss **monastic** **practices**, in particular, whether monks could be allowed to** handle money.**

 

**Third Buddhist Council :**

 
• It was held in** 250 B**C at **Pataliputra** under the **patronage** of** King Asoka.**
 
• It was presided by Moggliputta Tissa. The third part of the Tripitaka was coded in the** Pali language.**
 
• This Council appears to have met to compose commentaries on the **Tipitaka**.

 

**Fourth Buddhist Council :**

 
• The fourth Buddhist council was held in **72 AD **at **Kundalvana**, **Kashmir**.
 
• It was presided by **Vasumitra**, while **Asvaghosa** was** his deputy.**
 
• The council was held under the patronage of Kushan King Kanishka of the **Kushan Empire.**
 
• Buddhism was divided into two sects namely **Mahayana** and **Hinayana**.

 

**Fifth Buddhist Council :**

 
• The fifth Buddhist council was held in Mandalay**, Burma in the year 1871** under the patronage of **King Mindon.**
 
• It was presided by **Jagarabhivamsa**, Narindhabhidhaja and Sumangalasami.
 
• During this council,** 729 stone slabs** were engraved with **Buddhist teachings.**

 

**Sixth Buddhist Council :**

 
• The **Sixth Buddhist Council **was held in** 1954 in Burma at Kaba Aye, Yangoon.**
 
• It was held under the patronage of the Burmese government and it was presided by** Prime Minister U Nu.**
 
• The council commemorated **2500 years of Buddhism.**

questions.question: Which Turkish invader attacked and raided the temple of Somnath in 1025 AD?

__
 
• Turkish invader **Mahmud Ghazni**, attacked and **raided **the temple of **Somnath in 1025 AD**.
 
• The first of India's twelve sacred jyotirlingas is said to have arisen at the elaborately carved honey-colored Somnath temple or Deo Patan, is located in Prabhas Patan, Veraval in Gujarat, India.
 
 
• It is said that Shiva manifested there as a blazing column of light.
 
• The temples are situated where the Sarasvati, Hiran, and Kapila rivers converge, and the shoreline where they are built is touched by the ebb and flow of the Arabian Sea.
 
• Although the timeline of the ancient temple starts in 649 BC, it is thought to be older.
 
• Though it's difficult to see them through the foggy glass, vibrant dioramas depicting the Shiva narrative border the north side of the temple grounds.
 
• The temple was reconstructed several times in the past after repeated destruction by multiple Muslim invaders and rulers, notably starting with an attack by Mahmud Ghazni in the 11th century.
 
 
• The Pran-Pratistha at the existing temple was done on 11th May 1951 by then President of India, Dr. Rajendra Prasad.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Mahmud **invaded Gujarat **in **1025**, plundering the **Somnath shrine **and destroying its jyotirlinga. His loot included 2 million dinars. Somnath was conquered, and Anhilwara was invaded as retaliation.
 
 
 
• **Mu'izz ad-Din Muhammad**, also called **Muhammad of Ghor**, ruled the **Ghurid Empire** as its lone ruler from **1202 to 1206**, having served as its sultan from 1173 to 1202.
 
 
• He is credited with bringing about centuries-long **Muslim hegemony on the Indian subcontinent.**

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of six school of Indian Philosophy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dravida.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dravida** is not a school of Indian philosophy.
 
• Dravida is a term used to refer to the** southern part of India.**
 
• **Samkhya** is one of the **oldest schools of Indian philosophy** that focuses on the** dualism of matter and spirit.**
 
• It believes in the existence of **Purusha (consciousness) and Prakriti (matter)** and their interplay.
 
• **Yoga** is a school of Indian philosophy that emphasizes the practice of **physical, mental, and spiritual disciplines** to attain liberation or Moksha.
 
• It is based on the** Yoga Sutras of Patanjali.**
 
• **Nyaya **is a school of Indian philosophy that focuses on** logic and reasoning.**
 
• It aims to establish the validity of** knowledge and perception **through inference and deduction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian philosophy** is a vast field that encompasses various schools of thought, each with its unique approach and philosophy.
 
• The six schools of Indian philosophy are **Samkhya, Yoga, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Mimamsa, and Vedanta. **
 
• **Vaisheshika** is a school of Indian philosophy that focuses on **metaphysics and epistemology.**
 
• It believes in the** existence of atoms** and their combination to form matter.
 
• **Mimamsa** is a school of Indian philosophy that focuses on the interpretation of** Vedic texts and rituals.**
 
• It aims to establish the correct meaning and purpose of the** Vedic texts.**
 
• **Vedanta** is a school of Indian philosophy that focuses on the **Upanishads **and the concept of the **ultimate reality or Brahman.**
 
• It emphasizes the unity of the individual self or **Atman with Brahman.**

• **Dhammapada**
 
 
• The first discovery of the Prakrit text of the Dhammapada in Kharosthi was made in 1892 by the French traveller Dutreuil de Hhins, he also founded altogether three fragments in Khotan, which lie despatched to Paris.
 
• The Dhammapada is the only text of which a fragment has been preserved in Kharosthi, a script in which two recensions of Asoka's Rock Edicts, at Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra, are inscribed, and this is the only Buddhist text which has been hitherto found composed in a Prakrit dialect.
 
• The manuscript is one of the earliest finds from Khotan.
 
• Among later finds in Khotan, we have to mention a few documents containing dispositions and reports of local authorities, instructions, regulations, official and private correspondence — all inscribed in the Kharosthi script and drawn up in a Prakrit dialect.
 
• "Dhammapada," is a compound term composed of dhamma and pada.
 
• Dhamma refers to the Buddha's "doctrine" and Pada means "foot".
 
 
 
• **Prajnaparamita**
 
 
• Prajnaparamita Sutras and Vimalakirti Nirdesa Sutra are Mahayana Buddhist texts.
 
• The Prajnaparamita Sutras focus on the concept of 'perfection of wisdom' or 'prajna'.
 
• The Vimalakirti Nirdesa Sutra discusses profound aspects of Buddhist philosophy with a lay disciple as the protagonist.

• Three dynasties—the Chera, Chola, and Pandyas—ruled the Tamil nation during the Sangam Period. They were Muvendar, jointly as well.

• Variyar: Tax collector

questions.question: Rulers belonging to Gurjara - Pratihara, Rashtrakuta and Pala dynasties fought for control over _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kannauj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• **Kannauj, **as it was a strategic city located on the banks of the Ganges river and was considered the center of political power in North India **during the 8th-10th centuries.**
 
• Ujjain was an important city in ancient India and was the capital of the Gupta empire, but it had lost its political power by the time of the Gurjara-Pratihara, Rashtrakuta, and Pala dynasties.
 
• The Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty was based in Kannauj and ruled over a large part of North India from the 8th to the 11th century.
 
• The Rashtrakuta dynasty, on the other hand, was based in the Deccan region and had a strong presence in Central India. They often clashed with the Pratiharas for control over Kannauj.
 
• The Pala dynasty was based in Bengal and Bihar and had a strong maritime presence. They too were involved in the power struggle over Kannau Patliputra was the ancient capital of the Mauryan and Gupta empires, but by the 8th-10th centuries, it had lost its political significance.

questions.question: Which king inscribed the Hathigumpha (Elephant Cave) inscription in Udayagiri Hills, Odisha?
questions.solution:
• **Kharavela, the then Emperor of Kalinga**, inscribed the Hathigumpha (Elephant Cave) inscription in Udayagiri Hills, Odisha during 2nd century BCE.
 
• The Hathigumpha inscription situated near Bhubaneswar** gives information about year-wise achievements of Kharavela.**
 
• The inscription starts with a version of the auspicious Jain Namokar Mantra.
 
• The Inscription **consists of seventeen lines in deep-cut Brahmi script.**
 
• The contents of the Hatigumpha Inscriptions are taken as true records of Kharavela’s reign.
 
• The inscription gives a note on the political, religious, cultural and social condition of Kalinga during that glorious period.

questions.question: While Magadha was a powerful Mahajanapada, Vajji, with its capital at Vaishali (Bihar), was under a different form of government known as:
questions.solution:
__
 
• While Magadha was a powerful Mahajanapada, Vajji, with its capital at Vaishali (Bihar), was under a different form of government known as **Gana or Sangha**__.
 
• A gana or sangha had not one, but many rulers.
 
• Even if there were thousands of men who ruled, they were still called as Raja.
 
• All of them performed the rituals together and also met for assemblies.

questions.question: Where was the first Jain Mahasabha held?
questions.solution:
• The first Jain Mahasabha was held at **Pataliputra**(now known as Patna).
 
• It was held in the beginning of the **3rd century BC** by **Sthulabahu**.
 
• The second councils were held simultaneously at Mathura and Vallabhi and the third at Vallabhi.
 
• The Jain councils are associated with the revision and improvement of their sacred text termed as **Jain Agamas**.

questions.question: King Kharavela, the ancient Indian king whose biography is found in the famous Hathigumpha inscription, ruled from:
questions.solution:
